proposals.evidence: DEDR 1 lists the distal demonstrative paradigm, including Kannada ā/adu/atu, Kolami ad, Kota ad, Tamil avai and Kurux abṛā those things. These simple demonstrative forms are selected; compounds and the explicitly Pashto-influenced Brahui forms are excluded. Telugu anni/anta all are also explicitly included in this paradigm. User clarified on 2026-09-21 that each DEDR node represents the whole dictionary article, not only the displayed reconstruction. The head label remains unchanged; the cited article family/subsection is the proposed parent scope.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 410(b) explicitly lists Tamil iṉṟu/iṉṟaikku/iṟṟai, Malayalam innu, Kota inḏy, Toda ïḏ, Kannada indu, Kodagu indï, Tulu ini/inne, Gadaba ine(n), Kurux innā, Malto ine and Brahui ainō/annō today. These lexical temporal formations are cited to subsection (b), with the observed nṟ/nd/nn variants and Tamil-type dative temporal ending preserved; no unsupported separate day constituent is asserted. Per user clarification the node denotes the full article; its displayed heading remains unchanged. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
